column1: # Byte ceilings from the context-engineering charter, made checkable.
# AUTHORITY: src/user/claude-code/docs/context-engineering-claude-5.md, the
# "Byte reduction" and "Progressive disclosure for skills" paragraphs. These
# rows RESTATE that prose so a script can act on it; the charter remains the
# source of truth, and test_byte_ceiling_check.py fails if a row drifts from
# the number the charter states.
# Format: KIND<TAB>TARGET<TAB>CEILING_BYTES<TAB>NOTE
#   file      TARGET is one path; its size must not exceed CEILING.
#   sum       TARGET is a glob; the SUM of matches must not exceed CEILING.
#   each      TARGET is a glob; EACH match must not exceed CEILING.
# An `each` row may be excused per-file with an EXCUSE line (same reasoning as
# the parity manifest's #EXCLUDE rows: a deliberate exception must be written
# down, or it cannot be told apart from an oversight). The charter explicitly
# permits this for skills -- "no SKILL.md over 10KB WITHOUT A RECORDED
# JUSTIFICATION (format-authority tables that are themselves output contracts
# are the expected exception)".
#   Format: #EXCUSE<TAB>path<TAB>reason
# Warn-only by default; --strict makes it gate.
# SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH. The #EXCUSE lines below are authoritative for what is
# ratified. docs/migration/claude-5/baseline-metrics.md records the same
# justifications in prose and verification-report.md check A17 reads PASS on
# them; that prose is documentation, this file is the mechanism. When they
# disagree, this file is wrong until reconciled -- an earlier revision of this
# header claimed nothing was excused while the record already justified all
# thirteen, which overstated the breach count by an order of magnitude.
file
